newsitem.title: GERMANY: German A&A partner says not to merge with Aon.
newsitem.headline: German A&A partner says not to merge with Aon.

text.p: Jaspers Industrie Assekuranz (JIA), the German partner of the Alexander & Alexander broking group which was acquired by Aon on Wednesday, does not expect to be merged with the German AON operations.

"We have expected this situation and have prepared for it," joint managing director Stephan Zilkens told Reuters. "We will have to remodel our international network and find alternative solutions," he added.
"But there are binding contracts, which for the moment will be fulfilled," Zilkens said.
Alexander & Alexander owns 20 percent of JIA, Deutsche Bank 20 percent and three families the remaining 60 percent.
In September, Aon acquired the German broker Wesselhoeft Ahlers & Schues, in addition to its existing operation HAVAG/Hudig Langeveldt.

The newly combined German Aon operation is one of JIA's fiercest competitors. Market sources believe that Deutsche Bank is likely to make an offer to Aon/Alexander & Alexander for the 20 percent stake in JIA.
This could eventually lead to the bank aquiring the majority of the company. JIA expects for 1996 commission turnover of 90 million marks, on premium volume of 750 million marks.
Around 15 percent is international business via the A&A network.
